thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-9987 fired for service: model-serving-prod (high urgency) — triggered by cpu/mem saturation on gpu-cluster-3.

pagerduty: Paging user: @sre-oncall (primary rotation) and escalation targets. Incident link: https://pd.company/pd-incidents/PD-9987

elaine: ack'd. getting a popup — I'm oncall for infra, not model-serving-prod. looks like this is routing to the wrong service binding? :thinking_face:

mike: I'm getting the page too but my rotation says me for model-serving-nonprod. We recently applied a schedule override for contractor cover. Could be the override bled into prod binding.

jordan: I pushed a schedule-override PR yesterday to temporarily add contractors for weekend coverage, did `pd schedule-override add --rotation contractors --until 2026-03-14`. I intended nonprod only but might have hit the wrong service scope. Opening it now.

elaine: Production customers are seeing 503s on /v1/generate from the edge. I'm seeing a 20% error rate across GA region for the last 6m. We should assume customer impact until we confirm otherwise.

sre-oncall: I'm looking at the PD binding: `service: model-serving-prod` is bound to schedule `rotation-main` and also has an active override to `contractors` due to a mis-scoped apply. pdctl shows: 
```
> pdctl overrides list --service model-serving-prod
- override id: OV-778
  rotation: contractors
  scope: global (should be nonprod only)
  created_by: jordan
  expires: 2026-03-14T09:00:00Z
```

mike: yep that's the problem, overrides intended for model-serving-nonprod somehow used `--service '*'` in the tool. Jordan, can you revoke OV-778?

jordan: doing now. `pdctl overrides revoke --id OV-778`

ops: revoke response: `OV-778: revoked`

pagerduty: PD-9987: notified rotation changed. Recalculating current primary: @sre-oncall now correctly on primary.

sre-oncall: Confirming I've been paged and acked. Starting mitigation checklist: 1) confirm customer impact and scope 2) triage root cause (routing vs infra) 3) apply mitigation (rollback, scale, or patch) 4) communicate to CS/Support.

elaine: Quick checks: GPU hosts show high steal and OOM-like kills in k8s events for replicas of model-serving. But the timing matches override change ~10m earlier. Could be an automated deploy hit wrong pool?

mike: I'm pulling deploy logs: `deploy-service model-serving-prod` did not run in last 30m. No rolling restart. So likely not a deploy. The override probably caused oncall responders to run corrective automation that targeted nonprod pools by mistake — double-checking runbooks.

jordan: I see an automated runbook executed by contractors user: `repair-auto --target model-serving-prod --scale -2` at 2154319500. That was supposed to target nonprod. Undoing scale now: `kubectl scale deployment model-serving --replicas=12 -n prod`

ops: kubectl output: `deployment/model-serving scaled to 12`

elaine: Error rate falling to 5% now. Latency back to normal for most requests. Customers still affected if they hit the evicted pods; routing cache TTL 60s so should be stabilized within a minute.

sre-oncall: Good. We'll keep PD open until error rate <1% for 10m. For now setting PD status: acknowledged, mitigation in progress, severity: Sev2 (customer-facing degraded).

mike: For the PD binding fix: adding a guard to the override CLI to require explicit `--scope nonprod` when `--rotation contractors` is used. Filing a quick PR and patching the tool.

jordan: PR opened: https://git.company/pr/4257 — small validation, will backport to last tag.

elaine: Notifying support and CS: "We identified a mis-scoped schedule override that caused the contractor runbook to target prod -> temporary customer impact (some 503s). Mitigation applied, services stabilized, follow-up RCA in 2 hours." @support-team please post update to the status page. :email:

sre-oncall: Assigning follow-ups: 1) jordan - RCA + exact timeline (due EOD) 2) mike - patch CLI validation and emergency rollback playbook (due tomorrow) 3) infra - audit overrides for other services (due EOD). I'll create the incident ticket and mark owners.

pagerduty: PD-9987: status changed to acknowledged by @sre-oncall.

incident-bot: Incident PD-9987: timeline summary added. Postmortem required (sev2).

elaine: Closing note: please avoid using global scope when applying overrides unless explicitly intended. Also consider a require-2fa/approval for overrides that affect prod.

sre-oncall: Agreed. Wrapping up here — keeping channel open for RCA. :white_check_mark:
